:::{#exr-basis-size-practice}
#### Testing whether two vectors can form a basis of $\reals^3$

A list of two features cannot describe every point in $\reals^3$,
and @thm-basis-size says why in terms of [bases](#def-basis).
The [indicator vectors](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-indicator-vector) $\vecf{e}_1$, $\vecf{e}_2$ and $\vecf{e}_3$ form a basis of $\reals^3$.

Can a list of $2$ vectors be a basis of $\reals^3$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Use @thm-basis-size with the [basis](#def-basis) $\vecf{e}_1, \vecf{e}_2, \vecf{e}_3$.

:::
